calls.title: Zoro + GrowthBook
calls.summary: GrowthBook's meeting outlined a unified solution integrating feature flagging and experimentation for optimized product rollout. Key features include targeted rollouts based on user properties, robust deduplication, and exposure tracking for clean data. Upcoming enhancements in product analytics focus on warehouse-native exploration with SQL visibility and natural language querying. The platform also emphasizes meta-analysis for experimentation insights, aiming for improved financial impact assessments. Security is highlighted through self-hosting options and role-based access controls, while a simple pricing model targets enterprise customers. Customer feedback mechanisms are integrated to enhance usability and address specific concerns regarding metadata and financial tools.
calls.keywords: feature flagging, experimentation platform, product analytics, AI assistant, data warehouse, LaunchDarkly replacement

calls.title: Zoro + GrowthBook
calls.summary: Growthbook presented its vision for integrating experimentation, product analytics, and session replay into a unified platform aimed at providing holistic insights and streamlined workflows. Key features discussed included advanced capabilities for feature flagging and A/B testing, the introduction of session replay in beta, and an AI data analyst that enhances user interactions with data through natural language queries. Additionally, enhancements in funnel analytics and proactive AI insights were highlighted, aiming to simplify anomaly detection and reduce manual monitoring. The session replay tool, designed to correlate user behavior with experiment outcomes, was also discussed, alongside robust developer tools like a native browser extension and APIs for automating experiment workflows. Growthbook's focus on documenting experiment learnings and its differentiation through AI capabilities were emphasized to support continuous improvement.
calls.keywords: Growthbook, experimentation, product analytics, session replay, AI insights, warehouse-native

calls.title: Zoro + GrowthBook POC
calls.summary: The team aligned on the GrowthBook proof of concept, detailing the necessary technical setup, which includes SDK integration on both client and server sides, event streaming to Google Analytics, and a key focus on Datadog webhook viability for feature toggles. Feature evaluations target GrowthBook's tools, including browser extensions and rollback capabilities, emphasizing user traffic accuracy and performance metrics. Legal approval is the first step before kickoff, anticipated to take up to four weeks, after which the test organization will be quickly provisioned. Dedicated 24-hour support will be available throughout the POC, and project communication will involve regular check-ins. Finally, the POC serves as a comparison against Datadog, assessing feature parity and performance accuracy while highlighting GrowthBook’s flexibility through its modular API approach.
calls.keywords: POC, GrowthBook, Datadog integration, feature flags, experiment analytics, Terraform provider

calls.title: Zoro + GrowthBook
calls.summary:
# Zoro + GrowthBook
Date: 2026-08-21 | Duration: 35m

## Summary
The discussion centered on transitioning from an internal experimentation system to a managed platform, aimed at accelerating learning and reducing operational overhead through advanced analytics tools. Jay Shelllarson emphasized enhancing experiment speed and analysis using flexible statistical methodologies. The meeting also addressed pricing strategies, favoring a platform fee plus user-based model, while ensuring broad access to experiment results. Participants focused on technical improvements needed in the current fragmented system and set clear timelines for a five-week proof of concept, aiming to finalize contracts aligned with Q3 revenue goals. Highlights included the strategic importance of avoiding poor feature rollouts and fostering a culture of experimentation.

## Keywords
Experimentation, Product Analytics, Pricing Model, Feature Flags, Data-driven, Proof of Concept

## Action Items

**Christian Liebenow**
Work internally with Sales CRO Ryan to determine the more suitable pricing model between user-based and experiment-based approaches for Zoro, considering viewer license pricing fairness (26:40)
Continue progressing on MNDA and master SaaS agreement, clarifying data privacy/deletion and other legal points to ensure aligned contract terms for POC usage (28:34)
Follow up early next week with Jay.shelllarson to provide an update on pricing discussions and contracting status (34:59)

**Jay.shelllarson**
Coordinate internally with legal and procurement to review NDAs, master SaaS agreement, and Statement of Work (SOW) in preparation for POC and potential contract signing (33:48)
Oversee and manage internal approval of pricing and contract terms, ensuring that expectations about experiment volumes and cost structures are met before final commitment (33:48)
